html:
SMTO-EXE-0198 — SMTO can't use that file location for the PDF

GUID: 5905bb63-6b45-59da-b5b1-b3d9e18137a6
Slug: pdf-invalid-path
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The file location given for the PDF can't be used. It may be a web link or network share, outside the folder SMTO may use, or a save name with the wrong ending. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the PDF is a web link or on a shared network drive, download or copy it onto the Gateway computer first, then give SMTO that local path. PDF tools only open files stored on the Gateway computer, not links or network shares.
  2. Make sure the file is inside the folder SMTO is working in for this conversation, not elsewhere on the computer. SMTO refuses files outside the folders it has been allowed to use.
  3. If you named a file to save to, give it the matching ending: .pdf for a PDF, .png or .jpg for page images. A save name whose ending doesn't match the result is rejected so files aren't mislabeled.
  4. If the file is on a different Gateway computer, ask SMTO to copy it to this Gateway first. SMTO does not move files between computers on its own.

What success looks like

  • When you ask again, SMTO reads the PDF and shows its result or a new file under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file path you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change which folders SMTO is allowed to use just to get past this; let that person decide.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF path validation rejected the input or output path: a URL or network (UNC) path, a path refused by the Gateway file policy, or an output_path whose extension does not match the generated output.

What this means

  • PDF path validation rejected URL/network forms, a File policy/type failure or an explicit output suffix inconsistent with the staged output. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF path validation rejected URL/network forms, a File policy/type failure or an explicit output suffix inconsistent with the staged output.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the target-local path, artifact scope, current File policy and expected output extension.

How to fix it

  • Pass a path local to the selected Gateway (or an artifact-workspace:// URI from the current run); local_path rejects any '://' form and paths starting with '\' or '//', and File policy failures (outside the guard root, not a regular file) map to invalid_path. When setting output_path, its suffix must equal the generated extension (.pdf, .png or .jpg); cross-Gateway sources must be transferred explicitly first.
  • Use a permitted target-local file or current-run artifact-workspace path. Cross-Gateway sources require an explicit transfer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a permitted target-local file or current-run artifact-workspace path. Cross-Gateway sources require an explicit transfer.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended regular input and new output destination pass current path policy.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
